installIsolation: isolated venv at %TEMP%/mcp-sdk-gate-venv (created fresh via `python -m venv`, `pip install mcp` only -- never installed into the repo's own Python or any tracked requirements/lock file; the venv is outside the repo tree and not committed)
verdictReason: mcp==2.0.0 (the official Python SDK, pinned to the exact version released alongside the 2026-07-28 protocol) implements the stateless core, server/discover, and stdio transport correctly, and its TaskStatus enum values agree with the ratified 5-state Tasks lifecycle -- but it ships NO working implementation of the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension for protocol 2026-07-28. Every tasks/* method (tasks/get, tasks/cancel; tasks/update does not exist in the SDK at all) is 'deliberately absent' (the SDK's own source comment) from the live method-routing table for every protocol version the SDK knows, including the legacy 2025-11-25 revision where Tasks used to be core. A live stdio JSON-RPC round trip against a real MCPServer confirms this behaviorally: tasks/get, tasks/cancel, and tasks/update all return -32601 Method Not Found even when sent with a fully valid stateless envelope. The SDK does ship a generic, first-class extension-plugin framework (mcp.server.extension.Extension / MethodBinding) whose own docstring uses tasks/get as its illustrative example -- meaning a project COULD hand-build a Tasks extension on top of that framework -- but per this plan's own ruling ("it does not hand-roll a second task protocol"), that is out of scope for N1-Protocol. N0 (standalone Night Watch, no MCP Tasks) remains the path.
evidenceProbeTransport: real stdio subprocess (mcp.client.stdio.stdio_client spawning a real python.exe child running mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer.run("stdio")), not an in-process shortcut

planAssumptionFindings.assumption: the official MCP Python SDK version selected for N1 negotiates 2026-07-28 and implements the Tasks lifecycle required below
planAssumptionFindings.detail: The protocol-negotiation half is TRUE: mcp==2.0.0 negotiates 2026-07-28 correctly (stateless core, server/discover, stdio transport all genuinely work, ground-truthed by a live stdio round trip). The Tasks-lifecycle half is FALSE: the SDK ships zero working route for tasks/get, tasks/update (which does not exist in the SDK at all), or tasks/cancel at 2026-07-28 -- the extension was pulled from the SDK's 2.0.0 release entirely (SDK's own release notes: "Known gaps: The tasks extension (SEP-2663) is not part of this release."). Per program ruling 5 and this slice's own instructions, this is Plan contradicted for N1; N0 (standalone Night Watch) remains the path.
